title: Immigration agents search congresswoman Ilhan Omar's home
summary:
US immigration agents have searched the home of Minnesota Representative Ilhan Omar as part of a criminal investigation.
Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents "executed a judicially authorised search warrant" for the property in the Washington DC area, a US justice department spokesperson said.
The search "is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation", the spokesperson said, but no further details were given.
Omar, a Democrat and outspoken critic of President Donald Trump, described the search on social media as "an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement".

title: Home Office asylum AI flunks one in five accuracy checks
summary:
A 20-page investigation by the Open Rights Group (ORG) claims the department is pressing ahead with AI tools despite concerns about their accuracy, oversight, and promised efficiency gains.
The findings, based on Freedom of Information requests and correspondence with ministers, concern two systems used by Home Office caseworkers: Asylum Case Summarisation (ACS), which summarizes asylum interviews, and Asylum Policy Search (APS), a chat-style tool helping officials search country policy information.
REG ADThe government insists humans remain responsible for asylum decisions, but ORG questions how reliably caseworkers can spot mistakes in AI-generated information.
It says the average monthly number of initial substantive asylum decisions since April 2026 fell about 42 percent compared with the same period in 2025, while the mean time from interview to decision rose 29 percent.
The Home Office confirmed in August that expert testing had stopped, despite previously telling MPs that checks were continuing.

title: South Africa withdraws asylum directive after anti-migrant unrest — RT Africa
summary:
“The attempt to practically implement the judgement immediately led to serious consequences that could not have been foreseen in the Court order,” Home Affairs said in a statement.
South Africa has been gripped by months of violent anti-migrant protests, prompting accusations of xenophobia and diplomatic disputes with countries including Nigeria and Ghana.
Anti-migrant groups including March and March and Operation Dudula have demanded tougher immigration enforcement, blaming foreigners for crime, job shortages, and pressure on public services.
The government has since stepped up immigration enforcement under a five-point plan announced by President Cyril Ramaphosa to tighten border controls and overhaul immigration laws.
Despite those measures, protests escalated again last week as demonstrators demanded that refugee centers stop processing asylum applications.

title: Palestinians dream of returning home after Israel raids West Bank camps
summary:
Palestinians have been displaced from their homes in Tulkarem refugee camp and dream of returning home.
This West Bank camp he can see in the distance once housed a two-storey building comprising four apartments, each measuring 300 square metres (3,229sq feet), in which he and his extended family lived.
Everything changed for Fuad and his family on January 21, 2025, when Israel launched a military assault in the occupied West Bank dubbed “Iron Wall”, initially targeting the Jenin refugee camp.
Mass displacementData from UNRWA cited in a report titled, Destruction of Palestinian Refugee Camps in the Northern West Bank, stated that 33,362 Palestinians remain forcibly displaced from the three camps.

title: Abdi-Wali makes history as first Somali-born refugee in UK Parliament
summary:
Abdi-Wali makes history as first Somali-born refugee in UK ParliamentNewsFeed Abdi-Wali makes history as first Somali-born refugee in UK ParliamentNewly sworn-in Labour MP Sagal Abdi-Wali has made history as the first Somali-born refugee woman elected to UK Parliament.
She won London’s Holborn and St Pancras seat, vacated by former Prime Minister Keir Starmer, defeating Green Party leader Zack Polanski.

title: Nigel Farage says Reform will suspend the UK asylum system for five years and deport thousands of refugees if he becomes PM
summary:
Nigel Farage today pledged to ban anyone from being granted asylum in the UK for five years if Reform wins the next election.
The Reform UK leader re-ignited a proposal from earlier this year to suspend the asylum system for a full parliamentary term and declare void any applications in progress.
All asylum tribunals, legal refugee routes and resettlement schemes will be scrapped and a Reform government would not hear the around 90,000 outstanding asylum and humanitarian protection appeals and instead deport the claimants.
Reform says there is 'no mandate' for such schemes and that anyone who has arrived under them would be deported.
But Reform is now expanding the toolkit of measures for countries that would not be hit hard by such restrictions.

title: At least 139 dead as migrant boat from Djibouti to Yemen capsizes
summary:
At least 139 dead as migrant boat from Djibouti to Yemen capsizesNewsFeed At least 139 dead as migrant boat from Djibouti to Yemen capsizesAt least 139 migrants, including 15 children, have died and 84 remain missing after a boat carrying more than 300 people capsized off Djibouti en route to Yemen.
The disaster highlights the dangers of the Eastern Route, where more than 900 people died or went missing in 2025.
